Unicentric Castleman disease: The patient's presentation with a localized mass in the pancreatic head, histological findings of hyalinization of germinal centers, 'onion-skinning', and the presence of plasma cells are characteristic of Castleman disease, specifically the unicentric subtype given the absence of systemic symptoms and localized nature of the lesion.
Reactive lymphoid hyperplasia: The patient's lymphoid lesion with marked vascular proliferation, hyalinization of germinal centers, and normal distribution of T and B cell markers could also be consistent with reactive lymphoid hyperplasia, although the specific features mentioned are more suggestive of Castleman disease.
